subject: the cheap routing tier measured against the full planner, and the free-tier quota refusal that followed
provider_policy: cloud_free (WEATHERGPT_PROVIDERS default, chosen by the reader: free cloud models only, everything else frozen)

router_tier_measured.recorded_note: the run that produced these numbers printed them per turn while it ran; its JSON was overwritten by the later rate-limited run, so this file records the measured values with that provenance stated rather than restating them as a fresh capture

quota_refusal.probe: a direct provider call with a 20 s budget through the configured router
quota_refusal.error: ProviderUnavailable: No model provider could answer. openrouter: OpenRouter could not answer: HTTP 429 Rate limit exceeded: free-models-per-day. Add 5 credits to unlock 1000 free models...
consequence: every cloud-free call is refused until the daily quota resets (free-models-per-day) or the account is topped up
with the cloud-only policy frozen and no other provider enabled, a turn reports "No model provider could answer" honestly and holds its facts rather than answering from a weaker path
each refused turn now costs a bounded wait: 12 s for the first look, 45 s for the plan, 25 s for a written answer, instead of a two-minute retry loop
options_measured_or_stated: wait for the daily free-quota reset
add a small credit to the OpenRouter account (1000 free-model calls per day)
unfreeze the local model as a fallback (deliberately not enabled: the reader froze everything else)
run with the cheap first look off (WEATHERGPT_ROUTER=off) to lower the request count, which does not help once the quota is spent

limits: The quota state is a property of the provider account and the day, not of this workspace: the same code answered all six journeys earlier the same afternoon.
No number here is a service level; each turn is one measurement.
